title_en: Liu Yunwu v. Jinyuan No.1 Detachment of the Traffic Police Brigade of Taiyuan Public Security Bureau, Shanxi Province — dispute over administrative enforcement in road traffic management
ruling_gist_en: Building a service-oriented government requires administrative organs to strictly enforce the law to maintain social management order, while also taking into account the actual circumstances of the counterparty. When there is room for discretion in administrative handling, the method that causes the least damage to the legitimate rights and interests of the counterparty should be chosen as much as possible; the implementation of temporary control measures such as detention cannot replace the substantive handling of the case. If the administrative organ fails to handle the case for a long time without justifiable reasons, it constitutes abuse of power.
keywords_en: Administration; Administrative Compulsory Measures in Road Traffic Management; Retrial; Supreme People's Court; Shanxi Province; Natural Person; State Organ; Road Traffic Safety Law; Provisions on Procedures for Handling Road Traffic Safety Violations; Whether Vehicle Detention is Lawful; Whether Long-term Non-handling by Administrative Organs Constitutes Abuse of Power; Identification of Legal Source Certificate of Vehicle; Reversal of Judgment; Vehicle Detention; Engine Number Modification; Frame Number Discrepancy; Long-term Non-handling; Principle of Proportionality; Administrative Discretion; Clarify the Principle of Proportionality for Administrative Compulsory Measures; Standardize Procedures for Handling Detained Vehicles; Application for Retrial
full_text_en:
Liu Yunwu v. Traffic Police Detachment Jinyuan No. 1 Brigade of Taiyuan Public Security Bureau, Shanxi Province — administrative compulsory measure concerning road traffic management

[Ruling Summary]

The construction of a service-oriented government requires administrative organs not only to strictly enforce the law to maintain social management order, but also to take into account the actual circumstances of the counterparty. Where there is room for discretion in administrative handling, the method that causes the least damage to the legitimate rights and interests of the counterparty shall be chosen to the extent possible; temporary control measures such as detention cannot replace the substantive handling of the case, and where an administrative organ fails to handle the matter for a prolonged period without justifiable reasons, it constitutes an abuse of powers.

Administrative Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2016) Supreme Court Admin Re-Trial No. 5

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Liu Yunwu, male, born on November 5, 1952, Han ethnicity, residing in Lüliang City, Shanxi Province.

Agent ad litem: He Jun'ai (spouse of Liu Yunwu, the applicant for retrial), female, born on January 26, 1956, Han ethnicity, same address as above.

Agent ad litem: Liu Cui (daughter of Liu Yunwu, the applicant for retrial), female, born on August 2, 1981, Han ethnicity, same address as above.

Respondent to the Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Traffic Police Detachment Jinyuan No. 1 Brigade of Taiyuan Public Security Bureau, Shanxi Province, domiciled at No. 21 Yansheng Street, Jinyuan District, Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Yan Jinsheng, Captain of the Brigade.

Agent ad litem: Wang Jijun, lawyer at Shanxi Xinxuefu Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Zhongqing, lawyer at Shanxi Xinxuefu Law Firm.

Liu Yunwu, the applicant for retrial, brought a lawsuit against the Traffic Police Detachment Jinyuan No. 1 Brigade of Taiyuan Public Security Bureau, Shanxi Province (hereinafter referred to as Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade) concerning an administrative compulsory measure in road traffic management. Dissatisfied with the administrative judgment (2010) Jin Zhong Zi No. 75 rendered by the Shanxi High People's Court, he applied to this Court for retrial. After conducting a hearing and review, this Court issued the administrative ruling (2015) Xing Jian Zi No. 156 to transfer the case for retrial. After the transfer, this Court formed a collegial panel composed of trial judge Geng Baojian, acting trial judge Li Tao, and acting trial judge Li Weihua to hear the case. The trial has now been concluded.

The courts of first and second instance found the following main facts: In July 2001, Liu Yunwu purchased a Dongfeng EQ1208G1 transport vehicle through installment payment from Shanxi William Automobile Rental Co., Ltd., with engine number 133040, frame number 11022219, certificate of conformity number 0140721, and ultimately registered under the license plate number Jin A2XXXX. After Liu Yunwu paid the full vehicle price in accordance with the contract, the vehicle remained registered and affiliated with that company. On December 12, 2006, when Ren Zhirong, the driver hired by Liu Yunwu, drove the vehicle to the intersection of Heping Road and Xiyu Township in Taiyuan City, the duty police officers of Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade detained the vehicle on the grounds that it had not undergone annual inspection, and deposited it in a parking lot that same day. On December 14, 2006, Liu Yunwu brought the vehicle's driving permit showing the inspection date as December 13, 2006, to address the violation. During verification, the duty police officers of Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade found that the engine number and frame number of the vehicle were not visible. They then continued to detain the vehicle on the grounds that it was suspected of using counterfeit plates and that the engine number and frame number could not be verified, and orally informed Liu Yunwu to provide other lawful and valid documents. Although Liu Yunwu repeatedly sought assistance and provided relevant materials, Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade continued to detain the vehicle on the grounds that he could not provide proof of lawful origin of the vehicle. Dissatisfied, Liu Yunwu filed an administrative lawsuit, requesting the court to revoke the detention by Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade and return the vehicle. During the court proceedings, both parties, under the court's organization, cut and examined the welded area of the vehicle's frame number. The frame number revealed after cutting was GAGJBDK011022219, while the frame number recorded in the driving permit provided by Liu Yunwu was LGAGJBDK011022219.

The Intermediate People's Court of Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province, held at first instance: After Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade orally informed Liu Yunwu to provide other lawful and valid documents, Liu Yunwu failed to provide the corresponding lawful documents; therefore, the detention of the vehicle by Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade was legally justified. Since the detention of the vehicle constituted a factual act, procedural defects in the administrative enforcement process of Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade could not serve as a statutory basis for revoking the detention. Although Liu Yunwu provided a certificate issued by Shanxi Lüliang Dongfeng Automobile Technical Service Station regarding the replacement of the engine block, the unauthorized replacement of the engine and alteration of the engine number were prohibited by the relevant laws and regulations of China. Liu Yunwu had consistently failed to provide other lawful and valid documents for the vehicle; therefore, his claim for revocation of the detention and return of the vehicle could not be sustained. Accordingly, the court of first instance rendered the administrative judgment (2010) Bing Xing Chu Zi No. 3, dismissing Liu Yunwu's claims. Liu Yunwu appealed.

The Shanxi High People's Court held at second instance: Liu Yunwu did not dispute the detention of the vehicle by Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade on December 12, 2006, due to the vehicle's failure to pass annual inspection. The dispute centered on whether Liu Yunwu had provided proof of lawful origin of the vehicle and whether Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade should have promptly returned the vehicle. Regarding the vehicle's frame number, the number revealed after cutting and examination did not match the number recorded in the driving permit. As to the absence of an engine number, although Liu Yunwu provided a certificate issued by Shanxi Lüliang Dongfeng Automobile Technical Service Station concerning the replacement of the engine block, the unauthorized replacement of the engine and alteration of the engine number were prohibited by the relevant laws and regulations of China. Liu Yunwu had consistently failed to provide the corresponding lawful documents. In accordance with the then-effective "Procedural Rules for Handling Road Traffic Safety Violations," the detention of the vehicle by Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade was legally justified. Pursuant to Article 15 of the "Procedural Rules for Handling Road Traffic Safety Violations," Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade, as an administrative enforcement organ, could investigate the vehicle it considered to be of unknown origin. However, Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade had never investigated and had not made a timely disposition, which was inappropriate. Accordingly, the court of second instance rendered the administrative judgment (2010) Jin Zhong Zi No. 75: 1. Revoking the administrative judgment (2010) Bing Xing Chu Zi No. 3 of the Intermediate People's Court of Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province; 2. Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade shall, within 30 days after the judgment takes effect, handle the detained vehicle lawfully and respond to Liu Yunwu; 3. Dismissing Liu Yunwu's other claims.

In his application for retrial to this Court, Liu Yunwu requested the revocation of the final judgment of the Shanxi High People's Court, an order for the respondent to the retrial to return the vehicle, and an order for the respondent to compensate for losses including vehicle loss, vehicle operating loss, transportation expenses, attorney fees, medical expenses, moral damages, and lost work time. His facts and reasons were as follows: (1) The applicant for retrial was the actual owner of the vehicle. The vehicle identification number (VIN) of a motor vehicle consists of 17 characters, containing information such as the manufacturer, year, model, body type and code, engine code, and assembly location. The first character of the VIN is the country or region code, with the letter "L" indicating the vehicle's country of origin is China. The absence of the letter "L" was clearly due to carelessness during the cutting of the frame. The law does not prohibit the replacement of an engine; the vehicle owner only has an obligation to apply for a change of the engine number on the driving permit after replacement. The court of original instance erred in finding that the applicant for retrial could not provide lawful origin for the vehicle, constituting an error in fact-finding. (2) The respondent to the retrial failed to fulfill its statutory obligation to inform, did not issue a written notice, and constituted an omission. In such circumstances, the court of original instance concluded that the applicant for retrial should proactively provide lawful documents for the vehicle and bear the corresponding burden of proof, constituting an error in the application of law. (3) If it were determined that the applicant for retrial did not provide lawful documents for the vehicle, the detention period would not be subject to the 30-day limit. Therefore, the judgment of the original instance requiring the respondent to respond within 30 days was unfounded. Meanwhile, the respondent had already inspected the engine number and frame number, and the court of original instance's finding that the respondent "had never investigated and had not made a timely disposition" was also untenable. (4) The respondent initially agreed to release the vehicle after a 4,000 yuan fine was paid. However, because the applicant for retrial sent a journalist to retrieve the vehicle, the respondent refused to release it and has detained the vehicle to date. This caused the applicant for retrial to engage in prolonged litigation, resulting in brainstem hemorrhage and a grade III disability.

The respondent to the retrial, Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade, submitted a defense opinion: (1) After the vehicle was detained, although the applicant for retrial provided documents such as proof of origin, driving permit, and inspection certificate, the engine number and frame number are the only data to confirm the vehicle's identity and whether it is qualified, and also serve as the vehicle's identification documents. The applicant for retrial, without authorization, replaced the engine, altered the engine number, modified the frame by welding on steel plates, and welded the frame number between the new steel plate and the frame, causing a discrepancy between the documents and the vehicle, preventing its return. Even if ownership and lawful origin of the vehicle could be proven, the applicant for retrial would lawfully lose ownership of the vehicle. (2) Since the vehicle was in a continuous state of detention, the enforcement actions of the respondent concerned two violations—driving without annual inspection and driving a vehicle that has reached mandatory scrapping standards—and did not require two separate detention decisions. The respondent orally informed the applicant to continue providing valid and lawful documents, but the applicant for retrial never came forward to address the matter. (3) Due to the applicant for retrial's repeated petitions and lawsuits, the vehicle is still being kept by the respondent for evidence preservation purposes. It is currently a motor vehicle subject to mandatory dismantling and scrapping, and cannot be returned by law. (4) The applicant for retrial's unauthorized modification of the vehicle should be strictly cracked down upon and handled in accordance with the law. Therefore, the respondent's detention of the vehicle was lawful; the original judgment was basically clear in fact-finding and relatively accurate in the application of law, and the respondent requested this Court to dismiss Liu Yunwu's application for retrial.

During the hearing conducted by this Court in reviewing Liu Yunwu's retrial application, both parties expressed no objection to the main facts found in the original judgments, which this Court confirms.

Regarding the three certificates submitted by the applicant for retrial Liu Yunwu during the original proceedings—issued by Shanxi Lüliang Dongfeng Automobile Technical Service Station concerning the replacement of the engine block, the concealment of the engine number due to the engine block replacement, and the covering of the frame number due to reinforcement of the frame with steel plates and rivets—the respondent to the retrial, Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade, did not express any negative opinion on the authenticity of these three certificates during the hearing before this Court. During the retrial, this Court lawfully went to the service station to verify the facts, and the service station confirmed the three certificates. This Court requested Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade to present its opinion on the above evidence, and Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade stated that it would not express any opinion. This Court finds that the above three certificates are authentic, lawful, and relevant, and hereby accepts them as evidence.

This Court further finds that the frame number, also known as the vehicle identification number (VIN), generally consists of 17 characters of letters and numbers and is an important identifier of the vehicle. The first character is the country or region code, with China's code being "L". The last 8 characters, i.e., characters 10 to 17, represent information such as the vehicle's model year, production plant, and production sequence number. For a specific vehicle produced by a specific manufacturer, the string of the last 8 characters of the VIN is unique.

During the trial, this Court organized the parties to mediate concerning compensation, but due to significant differences between the parties, mediation was unsuccessful.

This Court holds: The focus of the dispute in this case is whether the administrative compulsory measure of detaining the vehicle by the respondent to the retrial, Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade, was lawful. Specifically, this concerns the following three issues:

(1) Whether the procedure for deciding to detain the vehicle was lawful. Pursuant to Article 96, paragraph 1 of the "Road Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China" adopted by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on October 28, 2003, and Article 13, item 2 of the "Procedural Rules for Handling Road Traffic Safety Violations" promulgated by the Ministry of Public Security on April 30, 2004, Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade has the authority to detain a vehicle if, during administrative enforcement, it discovers that the vehicle is suspected of using counterfeit plates. After the applicant for retrial Liu Yunwu submitted lawful annual inspection documents, Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade further discovered that the vehicle lacked an engine number and had an unidentifiable frame number, raising suspicion of counterfeit plates, and could lawfully continue detention. However, the decision to detain by Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade should comply with the administrative procedures prescribed in Article 112, paragraph 1 of the "Road Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China" and Article 11, paragraph 1 of the "Procedural Rules for Handling Road Traffic Safety Violations," including informing the party of the basic facts of the violation, the type and basis of the proposed administrative compulsory measure, and the rights the party is entitled to; hearing the party's statements and defenses; and producing and serving a written instrument of administrative compulsory measure. Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade violated the above administrative procedures by failing to issue any written detention decision, thereby breaching legal procedure. After Liu Yunwu provided lawful annual inspection documents, the initial detention by Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade on the grounds of failure to undergo annual inspection should have ended. Its claim that continuing detention on the grounds of suspected counterfeit plates did not require a separate detention decision cannot be legally sustained, and this Court does not support it.

(2) Whether the evidence was sufficient to support the continued detention on the grounds of suspected counterfeit plates. Comparing the vehicle's frame number revealed after cutting and examination (16 characters) with the frame number recorded in the driving permit (17 characters), the former lacked the first character representing the country or region of production. The applicant for retrial Liu Yunwu claimed that the missing first character "L" was inadvertently damaged during the cutting and examination, and the respondent to the retrial did not express a contrary opinion. Given that the vehicle was indeed produced in China, and for this model of Dongfeng transport vehicle, the last 8 characters of both the displayed frame number after cutting and the frame number in the driving permit were "11022219," it can be determined that the detained vehicle is the vehicle recorded in the driving permit held by Liu Yunwu. After Liu Yunwu provided purchase documents, an explanation from Shanxi William Automobile Rental Co., Ltd., three certificates from Shanxi Lüliang Dongfeng Automobile Technical Service Station, and other relevant materials, Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade's continued detention on the grounds of suspected counterfeit plates was based on insufficient primary evidence.

(3) Whether the failure to investigate and the prolonged detention of the vehicle constituted an abuse of powers. The engine number and frame number stamped on the vehicle body are important means of identifying the vehicle. Pursuant to Articles 9 and 10 of the "Regulations on Motor Vehicle Registration" promulgated by the Ministry of Public Security on April 30, 2004, Liu Yunwu's repair of the vehicle's engine and frame at a maintenance station designated by the vehicle manufacturer was not unlawful. Moreover, he merely replaced the engine block, not the engine itself. However, Liu Yunwu's failure to promptly arrange for the relevant unit to re-stamp the numbers at the corresponding locations and complete the necessary formalities was improper. Given that the engine number was not stamped on the replaced engine block and the frame number was covered by steel plates and rivets, making it invisible to the naked eye, Liu Yunwu was at fault for having his hired driver operate the vehicle on the road. Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade had the legal authority to detain the vehicle on suspicion of counterfeit plates, and Liu Yunwu should bear corresponding responsibility. However, vehicle detention is a temporary administrative compulsory measure and cannot be used as a substitute for substantive handling. After detaining the vehicle, Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade should, in accordance with Article 96, paragraph 2 of the "Road Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China" and Article 15 of the "Procedural Rules for Handling Road Traffic Safety Violations," take corresponding actions: If it considers that Liu Yunwu has provided corresponding lawful certificates, it should promptly return the motor vehicle; if it still has doubts about the proof of origin provided by Liu Yunwu, it should promptly investigate and verify; if it considers that Liu Yunwu needs to complete corresponding formalities, it should clearly inform him of the specific methods and procedures for completing the formalities and provide necessary assistance in accordance with the law. The driving permit and related annual inspection documents, purchase documents, the explanation from Shanxi William Automobile Rental Co., Ltd., and the three certificates from Shanxi Lüliang Dongfeng Automobile Technical Service Station successively provided by Liu Yunwu were sufficient to prove the facts that the engine block was replaced at a maintenance station designated by the vehicle manufacturer and that the frame was reinforced with steel plates and rivets. Under these circumstances, Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade neither returned the motor vehicle, nor promptly and proactively investigated and verified the vehicle's proof of origin, nor required Liu Yunwu to provide corresponding security and lift the detention to allow the vehicle to be returned to the maintenance station for rectification or to the original vehicle management office for re-stamping of numbers and completion of formalities. Instead, it repeatedly demanded that Liu Yunwu provide other lawful proof of origin that was objectively no longer available, thereby abusing the powers conferred by laws and regulations.

The process of administrative organs exercising social management is also a process of serving the public and protecting citizens' rights. The construction of a service-oriented government requires administrative organs not only to strictly enforce the law to maintain social management order, but also to take into account the actual circumstances of the counterparty. Where a counterparty, despite having some fault, has provided a reasonable explanation, and the administrative purpose can be achieved through multiple means, the method that causes the least damage to the counterparty's rights and interests should be chosen, provided the administrative purpose is sufficiently achieved. The implementation of administrative management should not solely consider the unilateral management needs of the administrative organ, but should be based on the principle of facilitating fact-finding without imposing additional burdens on the counterparty. The use of temporary control measures such as detention should be limited to stopping illegal acts, preventing destruction of evidence, and facilitating fact-finding; prolonged detention without disposition, causing unnecessary losses to the party, is impermissible. Therefore, after detaining the vehicle, Jinyuan Traffic Police No. 1 Brigade neither actively investigated and verified the vehicle's proof of origin, nor promptly handled the detention, constituting an abuse of powers.

In summary, when a people's court reviews the legality of an administrative act, it should comprehensively assess based on the evidence collected, facts determined, laws applied, and reasons asserted by the administrative organ at the time of making the administrative act. The vehicle involved in this case had passed its annual inspection and was being driven normally. At the time of making the administrative act and during the original trial and appellate proceedings, the Jinyuan First Brigade did not use the grounds that the vehicle had been illegally modified and should be compulsorily scrapped as reasons for impounding the vehicle, nor did it provide evidence during this court's trial to prove that the vehicle should be compulsorily scrapped. Therefore, the claim of the Jinyuan First Brigade that the vehicle should be compulsorily scrapped should not be supported. Moreover, changing the reasons for impoundment during the retrial also violates the basic requirements of administration according to law.

Therefore, when deciding to impound the vehicle, the Jinyuan First Brigade did not follow statutory procedures; the determination that the vehicle was suspected of using a counterfeit license plate and the continued impoundment lacked sufficient evidence; and neither investigating nor verifying and keeping the vehicle impounded for a long period constituted an abuse of power. Since the Jinyuan First Brigade did not issue a written impoundment decision, the impoundment act has no content that can be revoked. The people's court should, in accordance with Article 74, paragraph 2, item 1 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, confirm the impoundment act as illegal and order the return of the illegally impounded vehicle.

The first-instance judgment dismissing Liu Yunwu's claims was erroneous and should be reversed in accordance with law. The second-instance judgment failed to adjudicate on the legality of the impoundment act, ordered the Jinyuan First Brigade to handle the matter, and dismissed Liu Yunwu's other claims, which was also erroneous and should be reversed in accordance with law.

Given that Liu Yunwu has already filed a separate administrative compensation lawsuit regarding the losses from suspension of operation and vehicle damage caused by the Jinyuan First Brigade's impoundment, Liu Yunwu's compensation claims should be resolved separately in that administrative compensation case.

Accordingly, pursuant to Article 89, paragraph 1, item 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 78 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. Revoke the administrative judgment (2010) Jin Xing Zhong Zi No. 75 of the Shanxi High People's Court and the administrative judgment (2010) Bing Xing Chu Zi No. 3 of the Taiyuan Intermediate People's Court of Shanxi Province;

2. Confirm that the act of the retrial respondent, Jinyuan First Brigade of Traffic Police Detachment of Taiyuan Public Security Bureau, Shanxi Province, in impounding the vehicle with license plate Jin A2XXXX is illegal;

3. Order the retrial respondent, Jinyuan First Brigade of Traffic Police Detachment of Taiyuan Public Security Bureau, Shanxi Province, to return the vehicle with license plate Jin A2XXXX to the retrial applicant Liu Yunwu within thirty days after this judgment takes effect.

The case acceptance fees for the first and second instances, totaling RMB 100, shall be borne by the retrial respondent, Jinyuan First Brigade of Traffic Police Detachment of Taiyuan Public Security Bureau, Shanxi Province.

This judgment is final.
